_comment: Agent Robinhood bids' browser tools. AutolaunchWeb.ToolManifest adds them to tool_manifest.json only while the site offers agent Robinhood bids (AUTOLAUNCH_AGENT_ROBINHOOD_BIDS=true). The hosted MCP tools prepare_robinhood_bid and prepare_robinhood_bid_settlement take each tool's title and words from here, less how a browser host signs (Autolaunch).

tools.name: autolaunch_robinhood_bid_prepare
tools.title: Robinhood bid
tools.description: Prepare the wallet steps for one USDG bid on a Robinhood Chain auction, for one of my person's own wallets, built from the chain at the latest block as the auction page builds them: an exact USDG approval to the bid adapter (usdg_approval) while the wallet still needs it, then usdg_bid, which converts the USDG into the auction's stock through its admitted route, places the bid and returns what is left over in the same step, and reverts if the USDG buys less than min_stock_out or after its deadline, 15 minutes after block N. Each step is to, data and value for the wallet to send in turn on Robinhood Chain, the network chain names, its data ending with the site's Builder Code: the wallet must be on that network to send them. approved is true when no approval step is needed. Once the auction has ended bidding, by its record or the clock at the latest block, the answer is the refusal bidding_ended and no steps, and before that clock reaches the auction's start block the refusal auction_not_started and no steps. facts give the USDG spent, the stock it is estimated to buy and the least it must buy, the slippage, and the most per token after it is lowered to the auction's price grid. Built from block N: send the steps promptly, and prepare again once ten minutes have passed. The site only prepares: the wallet's own key signs and sends each step, and money moves only then; the bid joins autolaunch_my_positions once it is on the chain. Changes nothing. Signed: your browser host signs it with your own agent key, as regents browser does. Browser sign-in is not agent authority.

auction_id.description: The auction's id exactly as autolaunch_auctions lists it, for a Robinhood Chain auction.

usdg_amount.description: The total to bid in USDG, as a decimal with at most 6 decimal places. The bid converts it into the auction's stock and returns what is left over.

max_price.description: The most to pay per token, as a decimal in the auction's stock. It is lowered to the auction's price grid.

slippage_percent.description: The most the stock bought may fall short of the route's estimate, in percent from 0 to 99.99 with at most two decimal places. 5 when left out.

signer.description: One of my person's own wallet addresses, 0x and 40 hex digits. Omit it to use the wallet they signed in with.

tools.name: autolaunch_robinhood_bid_settlement_prepare
tools.title: Robinhood settlement
tools.description: Prepare the wallet steps that settle one of my person's own bids on a Robinhood Chain auction, by its bid id from autolaunch_my_positions, built from the chain at the latest block as the bid's row builds them: exit, which returns the unspent stock and records what the bid bought, then claim, which delivers the tokens once the auction graduated and claims are open; claim alone for a bid already returned; or, while bidding is open and the price has passed the bid's maximum but is not recorded yet, record, after which the return is prepared again. Only steps the auction would accept now come back; when there are none, the answer is a refusal naming the auction's reason. Each step is to, data and value for the wallet to send in turn on Robinhood Chain, the network chain names, its data ending with the site's Builder Code: the wallet must be on that network to send them. facts give the stock returned, the tokens bought and the tokens claimed. The auction pays the wallet that placed the bid, whichever of my person's wallets sends the step. The site only prepares: the wallet's own key signs and sends each step. Changes nothing. Signed: your browser host signs it with your own agent key, as regents browser does. Browser sign-in is not agent authority.

bid.description: The bid's id exactly as autolaunch_my_positions gives it (bid), for a bid on Robinhood Chain.

signer.description: One of my person's own wallet addresses, 0x and 40 hex digits. Omit it to use the wallet they signed in with.
